description: Kanhe protocol objects added in specification revision v0.7 (instances created by a call), built by an independent Python encoder from spec/kanhe.cddl and run by the reference interpreter tools/testvectors/wasm_ref.py. Two hand-assembled contracts: the splitting contract (split_contract in tools/testvectors/test_contracts.py: a receivable [amount, tier] held by {holder}, which splits into child parts and needs the holder's consent unless the holder is the home) and the v0.6 oracle contract (its byte-string arguments are its output; text aborts; anything else accepts with HASH(input) as the state). A registrar (a device; scope key 7: both contracts) and a clerk (a person; the oracle contract only) make calls; consents come from real party ledgers (on the home's hash), each with its complete evidence bundle. Statements are registered at t0 + 1000 + index; refused statements either break the CDDL (`malformed`) or are validated against the state after the first `after` statements, at t0 + 1000 + after; `why` names the rule (final, head, authority, depth, retired) or `contract` when the contract's run refuses it (its run says how). `runs` lists every contract run: the contract, the input the home builds (a child's instance view has key 6, [parent, depth]), and the outcome, output, fuel, and verdict. `children` lists each child's id, HASH([call, position]). `instances` gives each instance's final state (encoded), status, parties, head, finality, history, depth, parent, creating call's index, and position. `log_entries` holds the whole log, ending with the state commitment over `state_leaves`; `checkpoint` covers it. `evidence` holds the contract evidence (with the instance's evidence bundle) of three instances: one never split, a tier-3 part (with its ancestors' histories up to each split), and a child whose parent carried on after creating it; each with its depth, its ancestors (and the index of the call that made the next generation), the calls it shows (`events`), the log indices it holds (`entries`), the objects it proves (`involved`: the instance, its contract, then each event's signer, delegations, and grantors, in log order), and the consent bundles' hashes (`pins`). Signatures are Ed25519 (deterministic); keys are throwaway: seed = SHA-256("Kanhe test key: <name>"), and for party ledgers "<name> root" and "<name> log".
